headline: ৳71,495 crore: Govt to import LNG from US firm over 13 years
summary: The government has approved a proposal to import 78 cargoes of liquefied natural gas (LNG) from Gunvor USA LLC between 2026 and 2039.
details: The government has received policy approval to import liquefied natural gas (LNG) from the US-based private firm Gunvor USA LLC over a period of 13 years.
Based on current market prices, the total cost of the import is estimated at ৳71,495 crore.
The proposal was approved during an economic affairs cabinet committee meeting chaired by Finance and Planning Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury on Tuesday.
Under the government-to-government (G2G) arrangement, a total of 78 cargoes of LNG will be imported, with 6 cargoes arriving annually.
The import schedule is set to begin in 2026 and continue until 2039.
Petrobangla, under the Energy and Mineral Resources Division of the Ministry of Power, Energy and Mineral Resources, will implement the procurement process.
caption:

The proposal was approved during an economic affairs cabinet committee meeting chaired by Finance and Planning Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury on Tuesday.

Under the government-to-government (G2G) arrangement, a total of 78 cargoes of LNG will be imported, with 6 cargoes arriving annually.

The import schedule is set to begin in 2026 and continue until 2039.

Petrobangla, under the Energy and Mineral Resources Division of the Ministry of Power, Energy and Mineral Resources, will implement the procurement process.

headline_marked: LNG disruption causes [[gas crisis deepens for homes and industries]]
headline: LNG disruption causes gas crisis deepens for homes and industries
summary: Low gas pressure is forcing CNG stations in Dhaka to close one by one, while households and factories face severe shortages.
details: A deepening gas crisis is hitting Bangladesh, with LNG disruptions severely affecting both residential households and industrial sectors.
In the capital, low gas pressure has reached a critical point, leading to the gradual closure of several CNG filling stations across Dhaka.
The shortage is disrupting daily activities for residents and halting production in various factories that rely on gas for power.
Authorities are facing challenges in maintaining a steady supply as the disruption in Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) imports continues to strain the national grid.
caption:
Gas pressure is plummeting in Dhaka, forcing CNG stations to shut down and leaving homes and factories in the dark.

A deepening gas crisis is hitting Bangladesh, with LNG disruptions severely affecting both residential households and industrial sectors.

In the capital, low gas pressure has reached a critical point, leading to the gradual closure of several CNG filling stations across Dhaka.

The shortage is disrupting daily activities for residents and halting production in various factories that rely on gas for power.

Authorities are facing challenges in maintaining a steady supply as the disruption in Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) imports continues to strain the national grid.
